card.name: Punctuation and linking words mid-instruction
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods, commas, and small linking words (and, if, should, there, up) in drug-label instructions and warnings, right where a clause ends or a new one begins.

modes.label: Sentence-ending period
modes.description: A period closing a warning or instruction sentence.
modes.example: can precipitate serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition<<.>> The risk is increased with concomitant

modes.label: Linking word in a list or clause
modes.description: A word like and, if, or a comma joining steps or symptoms in a series.
modes.example: do not pressurize the flexible container to increase flow rates,<< and>> if administration is controlled by a pumping device

modes.label: Start of a new clause
modes.description: A word such as There, should, or up that opens the next part of a dosing statement.
modes.example: should not exceed 50 mg/min for Pentobarbital Sodium.<< There>> is no average intravenous dose of Pent
